"""A tiny JSONL-backed notes store.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * Notes live in a JSON-Lines file: one JSON object per line, in insertion
    order. The record shape is {"id": int, "title": str, "body": str,
    "created_at": str, "tags": [str, ...], "archived": bool}: add stamps
    "created_at" with an ISO-8601 timestamp (local time with its UTC offset,
    second precision), stores the tags given at add time as a list ([] when
    none were given), and marks the note as not archived ("archived": false).
    archive/unarchive flip that flag; list and find hide archived notes by
    default and only include them when asked (include_archived / --all).
    Tags are stored exactly as given at add time (no cleanup) and tag
    filters compare against the stored strings exactly, so "API Design"
    and "api-design" are different tags. Records written while the old
    tag cleanup was active already hold cleaned spellings such as
    "api-design"; nothing rewrites those records, and they keep matching
    by their exact stored form. search, added later, is the one place tags
    are compared forgivingly (see its docstring) and keeps doing so.
    New features should ADD fields to this record rather than replacing the
    format, and readers must tolerate records written before a field existed
    (e.g. pre-tag records have no "tags" key and read as untagged;
    pre-created_at records have no "created_at" key and read as dateless;
    pre-archive records have no "archived" key and read as not archived).
  * ids are integers assigned as (max existing id) + 1, starting at 1.
  * The whole file is small; loading it fully and rewriting it on mutation is
    the intended style. No indexes, no partial writes.

Public API (the CLI in cli.py is the supported interface; keep its commands
and its --file option working):
  NoteStore(path).add(title, body, tags=()) -> id
                       # tags is an iterable of tag strings; stored as a
                       # list, exactly as given (no normalization)
                       # also stamps "created_at" with an ISO-8601 timestamp
                       # and marks the note as not archived
  NoteStore(path).list_notes(tags=None, since=None,
                             include_archived=False) -> list[dict]
                       # no tags (or None/empty) and no since: every note
                       # that is not archived (or every note, archived ones
                       # included, when include_archived is True)
                       # tags: notes carrying EVERY given tag (exact string
                       # match against the note's stored tags)
                       # since: a "YYYY-MM-DD" date; keeps only notes whose
                       # created_at date (the date part of the stored
                       # timestamp) is on or after it. Records without
                       # created_at are dateless and never match a since
                       # filter. Raises ValueError when since is not a
                       # valid calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form.
  NoteStore(path).find(text, include_archived=False) -> list[dict]
                       # substring in title or body; archived notes are only
                       # returned when include_archived is True
  NoteStore(path).search(text, include_archived=False) -> list[dict]
                       # case-insensitive search, in file order: a note is a
                       # hit when the text (case folded) appears as a
                       # substring of its title or body, or when the text
                       # matches one of its tags -- both sides compared in
                       # normalized tag form (lowercase, strip, internal
                       # whitespace runs to "-"), so a tag's name, a messy
                       # spelling of it, or a fragment of it all surface the
                       # note, and tags stored messy by old records match
                       # too. Archived notes are only returned when
                       # include_archived is True.
  NoteStore(path).archive(nid) -> id    # flip the archived flag on: hide the
                                        # note from plain list/find. Raises
                                        # KeyError when no note has that id.
  NoteStore(path).unarchive(nid) -> id  # clear the archived flag on: the note
                                        # shows up in plain list/find again.
                                        # Raises KeyError when no note has it.
"""
import json
import os
from datetime import date, datetime


def _normalize_tag(tag):
    """Normalize a tag string to its canonical form.

    Lowercases the tag, strips leading and trailing whitespace, and
    collapses each internal run of whitespace down to a single "-", so
    "Python", " python " and "PYTHON  3" normalize to "python" and
    "python-3" respectively.

    This is search's tag-matching rule and nothing else: search keeps
    comparing tags this way so its behavior is unchanged, while add stores
    tags verbatim and list filters them exactly. The cleanup is no longer
    applied to stored tags or tag filters.
    """
    return "-".join(tag.strip().lower().split())


def _carries_all(note, tags):
    """True if the note carries every tag in ``tags``.

    Tags are compared exactly: each filter tag must equal one of the
    note's stored tag strings verbatim. Records written before tags
    existed have no "tags" key; they carry no tags, so they only match an
    empty filter. Records that got cleaned-up tags while the old
    normalization was active keep those spellings (e.g. "api-design") and
    match their exact stored form.
    """
    note_tags = note.get("tags", [])
    return all(tag in note_tags for tag in tags)


def _now_iso():
    """ISO-8601 timestamp for "now", in local time with its UTC offset.

    Used for created_at. The date part (first 10 chars) is the note's local
    creation date, which is what a list --since filter compares against.
    """
    return datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _created_on_or_after(note, since):
    """True if the note's created_at date is on or after ``since``.

    ``since`` is a normalized "YYYY-MM-DD" string, so comparing the date
    parts as strings is chronological. Records written before created_at
    existed have no "created_at" key; they are dateless and never match a
    since filter.
    """
    created = note.get("created_at", "")
    return created[:10] >= since


def _is_archived(note):
    """True if the note carries the archived flag.

    Records written before archiving existed have no "archived" key; they
    read as not archived, so they stay visible to plain list/find.
    """
    return note.get("archived", False)


class NoteStore:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = path

    # ----- persistence ----------------------------------------------------
    def _load(self):
        if not os.path.exists(self.path):
            return []
        notes = []
        with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if line:
                    notes.append(json.loads(line))
        return notes

    def _save(self, notes):
        with open(self.path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for n in notes:
                f.write(json.dumps(n, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    # ----- operations -----------------------------------------------------
    def add(self, title, body, tags=()):
        notes = self._load()
        nid = max((n["id"] for n in notes), default=0) + 1
        notes.append({
            "id": nid,
            "title": title,
            "body": body,
            "created_at": _now_iso(),
            "tags": list(tags),
            "archived": False,
        })
        self._save(notes)
        return nid

    def list_notes(self, tags=None, since=None, include_archived=False):
        notes = self._load()
        if not include_archived:
            notes = [n for n in notes if not _is_archived(n)]
        if tags:
            notes = [n for n in notes if _carries_all(n, tags)]
        if since is not None:
            try:
                since = date.fromisoformat(since).isoformat()
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise ValueError(
                    "since must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD form, "
                    f"got {since!r}"
                ) from exc
            notes = [n for n in notes if _created_on_or_after(n, since)]
        return notes

    def find(self, text, include_archived=False):
        return [
            n for n in self._load()
            if (include_archived or not _is_archived(n))
            and (text in n["title"] or text in n["body"])
        ]

    def search(self, text, include_archived=False):
        """Case-insensitive text-and-tag search, in file order.

        A note is a hit when ``text``, ignoring case, appears as a substring
        of its title or body, or when it matches one of the note's tags.
        Tag comparison is forgiving -- the one place tags are not matched
        exactly: both the query and each stored tag are passed through
        ``_normalize_tag`` (lowercased, stripped, internal whitespace runs
        collapsed to "-"), and the normalized query needs only to appear
        within the normalized tag name. So searching "errand" finds notes
        tagged "errand", searching "PYTHON  3" or "python 3" finds a note
        tagged "python-3", a fragment like "python" finds that note too, and
        messy tags stored by older records still match. Archived notes are
        only returned when ``include_archived`` is True (same rule as find).
        """
        lowered = text.lower()
        tag_query = _normalize_tag(text)
        hits = []
        for n in self._load():
            if not include_archived and _is_archived(n):
                continue
            if lowered in n["title"].lower() or lowered in n["body"].lower():
                hits.append(n)
                continue
            if tag_query and any(
                    tag_query in _normalize_tag(t)
                    for t in n.get("tags", [])):
                hits.append(n)
        return hits

    def _set_archived(self, nid, archived):
        """Set the archived flag on note ``nid`` and persist the change.

        Rewrites the whole file (the intended style for this store).
        Raises KeyError when no note carries that id.
        """
        notes = self._load()
        for n in notes:
            if n["id"] == nid:
                n["archived"] = bool(archived)
                self._save(notes)
                return nid
        raise KeyError(nid)

    def archive(self, nid):
        """Mark note ``nid`` as archived.

        Archived notes are hidden from plain list/find until unarchived or
        until a listing asks to include them. Idempotent: archiving an
        already-archived note keeps it archived. Returns ``nid``; raises
        KeyError when no note carries that id.
        """
        return self._set_archived(nid, True)

    def unarchive(self, nid):
        """Clear the archived flag on note ``nid``.

        The note becomes visible to plain list/find again. Idempotent:
        unarchiving a note that is not archived leaves it that way. Returns
        ``nid``; raises KeyError when no note carries that id.
        """
        return self._set_archived(nid, False)

"""Command-line interface for the notes store.

Usage:
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] add [--tag TAG ...] TITLE BODY
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] list [--tag TAG ...] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--all]
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] find TEXT [--all]
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] search TEXT [--all]
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] archive ID
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] unarchive ID

Design notes:
  * ``--file`` (default: notes.jsonl in the current directory) is the
    supported way to point the CLI at a different notes file; keep it working.
  * ``add --tag`` is repeatable; each tag is stored on the note exactly as
    given — no normalization or cleanup.
  * ``list --tag TAG`` (repeatable) shows only notes carrying every given
    tag, compared exactly against the stored tag strings (nothing is
    normalized on either side), so ``'API Design'`` and ``'api-design'``
    select different notes. ``list`` with no --tag keeps showing all notes.
  * ``list --since YYYY-MM-DD`` shows only notes created on or after that
    date, compared against the date part of the note's ``created_at`` field;
    ``list`` with no --since keeps showing all notes.
  * ``search TEXT`` matches case-insensitively against title and body
    (substring) and also against tags: the text is compared to the note's
    tags with the forgiving matching search has always used — the text and
    each stored tag are normalized for the comparison and the normalized
    text need only appear within the normalized tag (a tag's name, a messy
    spelling, or a fragment of either all match). This forgiving rule is
    search-only and unchanged; add/list match tags exactly.
    Archived notes are left out unless ``--all`` is passed. ``find`` keeps
    its original exact-case title/body behavior.
  * ``archive ID`` / ``unarchive ID`` flip the note's ``archived`` flag.
    ``list`` and ``find`` hide archived notes by default; ``--all`` on
    either command includes them again. archive/unarchive act by id and work
    whether or not the note is currently archived; a missing id is an error.
  * Notes print one line per note as "[<id>] <title> :: <body>"; keep the
    one-line-per-note shape so output stays grep-able.
"""
import argparse

from .store import NoteStore


def print_notes(notes):
    for n in notes:
        print(f"[{n['id']}] {n['title']} :: {n['body']}")


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="notes")
    parser.add_argument("--file", default="notes.jsonl")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_add = sub.add_parser("add", help="add a note")
    p_add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[],
                       metavar="TAG", help="tag the note (repeatable)")
    p_add.add_argument("title")
    p_add.add_argument("body")

    p_list = sub.add_parser("list", help="list notes")
    p_list.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=None,
                        metavar="TAG",
                        help="only show notes carrying this tag (repeatable)")
    p_list.add_argument("--since", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", default=None,
                        help="only show notes created on or after this date")
    p_list.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                        help="include archived notes")

    p_find = sub.add_parser("find", help="find notes by substring")
    p_find.add_argument("text")
    p_find.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                        help="include archived notes")

    p_search = sub.add_parser(
        "search", help="search notes (case-insensitive; matches tags too)")
    p_search.add_argument("text")
    p_search.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                          help="include archived notes")

    p_archive = sub.add_parser("archive", help="archive a note by id")
    p_archive.add_argument("id", type=int, metavar="ID",
                           help="id of the note to archive")

    p_unarchive = sub.add_parser("unarchive", help="unarchive a note by id")
    p_unarchive.add_argument("id", type=int, metavar="ID",
                             help="id of the note to unarchive")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    store = NoteStore(args.file)

    if args.cmd == "add":
        nid = store.add(args.title, args.body, tags=args.tag)
        print(f"added {nid}")
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        try:
            print_notes(store.list_notes(tags=args.tag, since=args.since,
                                         include_archived=args.all))
        except ValueError as exc:
            parser.error(str(exc))
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        print_notes(store.find(args.text, include_archived=args.all))
    elif args.cmd == "search":
        print_notes(store.search(args.text, include_archived=args.all))
    elif args.cmd == "archive":
        try:
            store.archive(args.id)
        except KeyError:
            parser.error(f"no note with id {args.id}")
        print(f"archived {args.id}")
    elif args.cmd == "unarchive":
        try:
            store.unarchive(args.id)
        except KeyError:
            parser.error(f"no note with id {args.id}")
        print(f"unarchived {args.id}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# notes

A tiny JSONL-backed note-taking CLI, used as a teaching toy.

Current capabilities:

    python -m notes.cli add [--tag TAG ...] "title" "body"               # append a note
    python -m notes.cli list [--tag TAG ...] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--all] # show notes
    python -m notes.cli find TEXT [--all]                                # substring match in title/body
    python -m notes.cli search TEXT [--all]                              # case-insensitive text & tag search
    python -m notes.cli archive ID                                       # hide a note
    python -m notes.cli unarchive ID                                     # show a note again

Notes carry tags: `add --tag TAG` is repeatable and stores each tag in the
note's `tags` list exactly as given (an empty list when no `--tag` is
given). `list --tag TAG` is also repeatable and shows only notes carrying
every given tag, compared exactly against the stored strings — so
`'API Design'` and `'api-design'` are different tags. Plain `list` still
shows all notes.

Tags are never rewritten: a note tagged while the old normalization was
active keeps its cleaned spelling (e.g. `api-design`) on disk, and
`list --tag api-design` finds it by that exact stored form.

Every note also records when it was created in a `created_at` field: an
ISO-8601 timestamp (local time with its UTC offset) stamped at add time.
`list --since YYYY-MM-DD` shows only notes created on or after that date,
compared against the date part of `created_at` (the date itself is
included). Records written before `created_at` existed have no timestamp and
never match a `--since` filter; plain `list` still shows all notes.

`search TEXT` finds notes whose title or body contains the text (substring
match, ignoring case) and also finds notes by tag: a note surfaces when the
search text matches one of its tags, with the same forgiving tag matching
search has always used — the text and each stored tag are normalized for
the comparison (lowercased, whitespace runs collapsed to `-`) and the
normalized text need only appear within the normalized tag name. So
`search 'PYTHON  3'` or `search 'python 3'` still finds a note tagged
`python-3`, a fragment such as `search 'python'` finds it too, and messy
spellings — from older records or from verbatim tags like `'API Design'` —
still match (e.g. `search 'api design'` finds a note tagged `'API Design'`).
This forgiving rule applies only inside search; `add` and `list --tag`
store and match tags exactly, as described above. Archived notes are left
out of search results unless `--all` is passed. The original `find TEXT`
keeps its exact, case-sensitive title/body behavior.

Every note has an `archived` flag (new notes start unarchived). `archive ID`
hides a note without deleting it; `unarchive ID` brings it back. Archived
notes are left out of plain `list` and `find`; pass `--all` to either
command to include them again. Records written before `archived` existed
have no flag and count as not archived. The flag composes with the other
filters, so e.g. `list --tag errand` also skips archived notes while
`list --all --tag errand` includes them.

Notes are stored one-JSON-object-per-line in `notes.jsonl` (override with
`--file`). See `notes/store.py` for the design notes. New features should add
fields to the note record rather than changing the storage format.

"""Tests for note tagging (add --tag / tags field / list --tag filter)."""
import contextlib
import io
import os
import tempfile

from notes.cli import main
from notes.store import NoteStore


def _store():
    d = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    s = NoteStore(os.path.join(d.name, "n.jsonl"))
    return d, s


def test_add_without_tags_stores_empty_list():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("plain", "no tags")
        assert s.list_notes()[0]["tags"] == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_add_with_tags_stores_them():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("work", "todo", tags=["work", "urgent"])
        n = s.list_notes()[0]
        assert n["tags"] == ["work", "urgent"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_list_filter_by_single_tag():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("a", "one", tags=["work"])
        s.add("b", "two", tags=["personal"])
        s.add("c", "three", tags=["work", "urgent"])
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes(tags=["work"])] == ["a", "c"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes(tags=["urgent"])] == ["c"]
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["nope"]) == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_list_filter_requires_every_given_tag():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("both", "x", tags=["work", "urgent"])
        s.add("only-one", "y", tags=["work"])
        hits = s.list_notes(tags=["work", "urgent"])
        assert [n["title"] for n in hits] == ["both"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_list_without_filter_still_shows_all():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("tagged", "x", tags=["work"])
        s.add("plain", "y")
        assert len(s.list_notes()) == 2
        assert len(s.list_notes(tags=None)) == 2
        assert len(s.list_notes(tags=[])) == 2
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_old_records_without_tags_field_are_tolerated():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        # A record written before the tags field existed.
        with open(s.path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write('{"id": 1, "title": "old", "body": "pre-tag"}\n')
        assert s.list_notes()[0]["title"] == "old"  # no KeyError
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["work"]) == []    # carries no tags
        # New adds coexist and still assign ids past the old record.
        assert s.add("new", "x", tags=["work"]) == 2
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def _cli(*argv):
    out = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
        main(list(argv))
    return out.getvalue()


def test_cli_add_and_list_filter_with_tag():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        path = s.path
        assert "added 1" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "buy milk",
                                 "from the shop", "--tag", "errand")
        assert "added 2" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "call mom",
                                 "this weekend", "--tag", "errand",
                                 "--tag", "family")
        assert "added 3" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "read book",
                                 "chapter 3")

        all_notes = _cli("--file", path, "list")
        assert "[1] buy milk" in all_notes
        assert "[3] read book" in all_notes

        errands = _cli("--file", path, "list", "--tag", "errand")
        assert "[1] buy milk" in errands
        assert "[2] call mom" in errands
        assert "read book" not in errands

        both = _cli("--file", path, "list", "--tag", "errand", "--tag", "family")
        assert "[2] call mom" in both
        assert "buy milk" not in both

        # find is untouched by tagging
        assert "[3] read book" in _cli("--file", path, "find", "chapter")
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_add_stores_tags_exactly_as_given():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        # No cleanup: tags keep their case and their spaces verbatim.
        s.add("a", "one", tags=["API Design", " Python ", "PYTHON  3"])
        assert s.list_notes()[0]["tags"] == ["API Design", " Python ",
                                             "PYTHON  3"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_list_filter_matches_stored_tags_exactly():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("a", "one", tags=["API Design"])   # stored verbatim
        s.add("b", "two", tags=["api-design"])   # a different tag
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes(tags=["API Design"])] == ["a"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes(tags=["api-design"])] == ["b"]
        # The filter side is exact too: no collapsing, no lowercasing.
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["API   Design"]) == []
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["api design"]) == []
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["nope"]) == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_exact_multi_tag_filter_requires_all_tags():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("both", "x", tags=["Work", "Urgent"])
        s.add("only-one", "y", tags=["Work"])
        hits = s.list_notes(tags=["Work", "Urgent"])
        assert [n["title"] for n in hits] == ["both"]
        # Case variants no longer collapse onto the stored tags.
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["WORK", "urgent"]) == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_cleaned_up_records_keep_tags_and_match_by_stored_form():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        # A record written while the old normalization was active holds the
        # cleaned spelling; nothing rewrites it, so it keeps that tag and is
        # found by its exact stored form.
        with open(s.path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write('{"id": 1, "title": "old", "body": "x",'
                    ' "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",'
                    ' "tags": ["api-design", "my-tag"]}\n'
                    '{"id": 2, "title": "plain", "body": "y",'
                    ' "created_at": "2026-01-02T00:00:00+00:00"}\n')
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes()] == ["old", "plain"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes(tags=["api-design"])] == ["old"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.list_notes(
            tags=["api-design", "my-tag"])] == ["old"]
        # The un-normalized spelling is a different tag now.
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["API Design"]) == []
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["api design"]) == []
        # Untagged records never match a tag filter.
        assert s.list_notes(tags=["plain"]) == []
        # New adds coexist and still assign ids past the old records.
        assert s.add("new", "x") == 3
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_cli_add_and_list_tags_exactly_end_to_end():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        path = s.path
        assert "added 1" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "design doc",

        assert _cli("--file", path, "list", "--tag",
                    "api-design").strip() == ""
        # find is untouched by tagging.
        assert "[1] design doc" in _cli("--file", path, "find", "API")
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    import traceback

    failed = 0
    for name, fn in sorted(globals().items()):

"""Tests for search (case-insensitive text + forgiving tag matching)."""
import contextlib
import io
import os
import tempfile

from notes.cli import main
from notes.store import NoteStore


def _store():
    d = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    s = NoteStore(os.path.join(d.name, "n.jsonl"))
    return d, s


def test_search_matches_title_case_insensitively():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("Buy Milk", "corner shop")
        s.add("call mom", "this weekend")
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("milk")] == ["Buy Milk"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("MILK")] == ["Buy Milk"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("Call")] == ["call mom"]
        assert s.search("zzz") == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_search_matches_body_case_insensitively():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("gym", "Leg Day!")
        s.add("read", "chapter 3 of the book")
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("leg day")] == ["gym"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("DAY")] == ["gym"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("CHAPTER")] == ["read"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_search_finds_notes_by_tag_name():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        # The query appears in neither title nor body: only the tag matches.
        s.add("buy milk", "from the shop")
        s.add("call mom", "this weekend", tags=["family", "errand"])
        s.add("read book", "chapter three", tags=["errand"])
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("errand")] == [
            "call mom", "read book"]
        # A tag name no note carries matches nothing.
        assert s.search("urgent") == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_search_tag_matching_is_forgiving_and_finds_fragments():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        # add stores tags verbatim now; search still normalizes both sides
        # of its tag comparison, so these messy spellings keep matching.
        s.add("note a", "x", tags=[" Python  3 "])
        s.add("note b", "y", tags=["My  Tag "])
        # The tag's canonical name, a messy whitespace spelling of it, and
        # even a fragment of the name all surface the note.
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("python-3")] == ["note a"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("python 3")] == ["note a"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search(" PYTHON   3 ")] == ["note a"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("python")] == ["note a"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("my-tag")] == ["note b"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("MY TAG")] == ["note b"]
        # Tags of different notes do not cross-match.
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("my")] == ["note b"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_search_finds_legacy_messy_tags():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        # Records may hold messy spellings (add stores tags verbatim, and
        # records written during the old cleanup keep their cleaned forms);
        # search must still find them by tag.
        with open(s.path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write('{"id": 1, "title": "old", "body": "pre",'
                    ' "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",'
                    ' "tags": [" Python ", "PYTHON  3"]}\n'
                    '{"id": 2, "title": "second", "body": "post",'
                    ' "created_at": "2026-01-02T00:00:00+00:00",'
                    ' "archived": false}\n')
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("python")] == ["old"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("PYTHON 3")] == ["old"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("python-3")] == ["old"]
        # Untagged records never match a tag query.
        assert s.search("urgent") == []
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_archived_notes_stay_out_of_search_unless_included():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("buy milk", "corner shop", tags=["errand"])
        s.add("call mom", "this weekend", tags=["errand"])
        s.add("read book", "chapter three")
        s.archive(2)
        # Text search skips the archived note ...
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("mom")] == []
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search(
            "mom", include_archived=True)] == ["call mom"]
        # ... and so does tag search.
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("errand")] == ["buy milk"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search(
            "errand", include_archived=True)] == ["buy milk", "call mom"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_search_results_keep_file_order_and_list_each_note_once():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("read book", "chapter 3")
        s.add("call mom", "this weekend", tags=["errand"])
        s.add("buy milk", "from the shop", tags=["errand"])
        # note 3 matches by text and by tag, but is listed once.
        assert [n["id"] for n in s.search("milk")] == [3]
        assert [n["id"] for n in s.search("errand")] == [2, 3]
        assert [n["id"] for n in s.search("book")] == [1]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def test_find_keeps_exact_case_behavior():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        s.add("Buy Milk", "corner shop")
        # find stays an exact-case substring match; search is not.
        assert s.find("milk") == []
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.search("milk")] == ["Buy Milk"]
        assert [n["title"] for n in s.find("Milk")] == ["Buy Milk"]
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


def _cli(*argv):
    out = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
        main(list(argv))
    return out.getvalue()


def test_cli_search_end_to_end():
    d, s = _store()
    try:
        path = s.path
        assert "added 1" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "Buy Milk",
                                 "corner shop")
        assert "added 2" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "call mom",
                                 "this weekend", "--tag", "errand",
                                 "--tag", "family")
        assert "added 3" in _cli("--file", path, "add", "read book",
                                 "chapter three", "--tag", "errand")
        assert "archived 2" in _cli("--file", path, "archive", "2")

        # Case-insensitive text match on title/body.
        by_text = _cli("--file", path, "search", "MILK")
        assert "[1] Buy Milk" in by_text
        assert "read book" not in by_text
        by_body = _cli("--file", path, "search", "CHAPTER")
        assert "[3] read book" in by_body

        # Tag search: "errand" appears in no title or body.
        by_tag = _cli("--file", path, "search", "errand")
        assert "[3] read book" in by_tag
        assert "call mom" not in by_tag     # note 2 is archived

        by_tag_all = _cli("--file", path, "search", "errand", "--all")
        assert "[2] call mom" in by_tag_all
        assert "[3] read book" in by_tag_all

        # Archived notes need --all even for plain text matches.
        assert "call mom" not in _cli("--file", path, "search", "mom")
        assert "[2] call mom" in _cli("--file", path, "search", "mom",
                                      "--all")

        # No hits prints nothing (and exits cleanly).
        assert _cli("--file", path, "search", "zzz").strip() == ""

        # find is untouched: still exact-case, still hides archived notes.
        assert _cli("--file", path, "find", "milk") == ""
        assert "[1] Buy Milk" in _cli("--file", path, "find", "Milk")
    finally:
        d.cleanup()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    import traceback

    failed = 0
    for name, fn in sorted(globals().items()):
        if name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn):
            try:
                fn()
                print(f"{name} ok")
            except Exception:
                failed += 1
                traceback.print_exc()
                print(f"{name} FAILED")
    if failed:
        sys.exit(1)
    print("search tests ok")

"""A tiny JSONL-backed notes store.

Design notes (READ THIS before changing behavior):
  * Notes live in a JSON-Lines file: one JSON object per line, in insertion
    order. The record shape is {"id": int, "title": str, "body": str,
    "created_at": str, "tags": [str, ...], "archived": bool}: add stamps
    "created_at" with an ISO-8601 timestamp (local time with its UTC offset,
    second precision), stores the tags given at add time as a list ([] when
    none were given), and marks the note as not archived ("archived": false).
    archive/unarchive flip that flag; list and find hide archived notes by
    default and only include them when asked (include_archived / --all).
    Tags are stored exactly as given at add time (no cleanup) and tag
    filters compare against the stored strings exactly, so "API Design"
    and "api-design" are different tags. Records written while the old
    tag cleanup was active already hold cleaned spellings such as
    "api-design"; nothing rewrites those records on its own, and they keep
    matching by their exact stored form (rename_tag below is the one
    explicit tag rewrite, and it compares and stores exactly too). search,
    added later, is the one place tags are compared forgivingly (see its
    docstring) and keeps doing so.
    New features should ADD fields to this record rather than replacing the
    format, and readers must tolerate records written before a field existed
    (e.g. pre-tag records have no "tags" key and read as untagged;
    pre-created_at records have no "created_at" key and read as dateless;
    pre-archive records have no "archived" key and read as not archived).
  * ids are integers assigned as (max existing id) + 1, starting at 1.
  * The whole file is small; loading it fully and rewriting it on mutation is
    the intended style. No indexes, no partial writes.

Public API (the CLI in cli.py is the supported interface; keep its commands
and its --file option working):
  NoteStore(path).add(title, body, tags=()) -> id
                       # tags is an iterable of tag strings; stored as a
                       # list, exactly as given (no normalization)
                       # also stamps "created_at" with an ISO-8601 timestamp
                       # and marks the note as not archived
  NoteStore(path).list_notes(tags=None, since=None,
                             include_archived=False) -> list[dict]
                       # no tags (or None/empty) and no since: every note
                       # that is not archived (or every note, archived ones
                       # included, when include_archived is True)
                       # tags: notes carrying EVERY given tag (exact string
                       # match against the note's stored tags)
                       # since: a "YYYY-MM-DD" date; keeps only notes whose
                       # created_at date (the date part of the stored
                       # timestamp) is on or after it. Records without
                       # created_at are dateless and never match a since
                       # filter. Raises ValueError when since is not a
                       # valid calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form.
  NoteStore(path).find(text, include_archived=False) -> list[dict]
                       # substring in title or body; archived notes are only
                       # returned when include_archived is True
  NoteStore(path).search(text, include_archived=False) -> list[dict]
                       # case-insensitive search, in file order: a note is a
                       # hit when the text (case folded) appears as a
                       # substring of its title or body, or when the text
                       # matches one of its tags -- both sides compared in
                       # normalized tag form (lowercase, strip, internal
                       # whitespace runs to "-"), so a tag's name, a messy
                       # spelling of it, or a fragment of it all surface the
                       # note, and tags stored messy by old records match
                       # too. Archived notes are only returned when
                       # include_archived is True.
  NoteStore(path).archive(nid) -> id    # flip the archived flag on: hide the
                                        # note from plain list/find. Raises
                                        # KeyError when no note has that id.
  NoteStore(path).unarchive(nid) -> id  # clear the archived flag on: the note
                                        # shows up in plain list/find again.
                                        # Raises KeyError when no note has it.
  NoteStore(path).rename_tag(old, new) -> int
                       # rename a tag on every note in the file, archived
                       # ones included: wherever a stored tag equals old
                       # exactly as stored, it is replaced with new exactly
                       # as given (no cleanup, no case folding); returns how
                       # many notes were changed, rewriting the file only
                       # when at least one did
"""
import json
import os
from datetime import date, datetime


def _normalize_tag(tag):
    """Normalize a tag string to its canonical form.

    Lowercases the tag, strips leading and trailing whitespace, and
    collapses each internal run of whitespace down to a single "-", so
    "Python", " python " and "PYTHON  3" normalize to "python" and
    "python-3" respectively.

    This is search's tag-matching rule and nothing else: search keeps
    comparing tags this way so its behavior is unchanged, while add stores
    tags verbatim and list filters them exactly. The cleanup is no longer
    applied to stored tags or tag filters.
    """
    return "-".join(tag.strip().lower().split())


def _carries_all(note, tags):
    """True if the note carries every tag in ``tags``.

    Tags are compared exactly: each filter tag must equal one of the
    note's stored tag strings verbatim. Records written before tags
    existed have no "tags" key; they carry no tags, so they only match an
    empty filter. Records that got cleaned-up tags while the old
    normalization was active keep those spellings (e.g. "api-design") and
    match their exact stored form.
    """
    note_tags = note.get("tags", [])
    return all(tag in note_tags for tag in tags)


def _now_iso():
    """ISO-8601 timestamp for "now", in local time with its UTC offset.

    Used for created_at. The date part (first 10 chars) is the note's local
    creation date, which is what a list --since filter compares against.
    """
    return datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _created_on_or_after(note, since):
    """True if the note's created_at date is on or after ``since``.

    ``since`` is a normalized "YYYY-MM-DD" string, so comparing the date
    parts as strings is chronological. Records written before created_at
    existed have no "created_at" key; they are dateless and never match a
    since filter.
    """
    created = note.get("created_at", "")
    return created[:10] >= since


def _is_archived(note):
    """True if the note carries the archived flag.

    Records written before archiving existed have no "archived" key; they
    read as not archived, so they stay visible to plain list/find.
    """
    return note.get("archived", False)


class NoteStore:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = path

    # ----- persistence ----------------------------------------------------
    def _load(self):
        if not os.path.exists(self.path):
            return []
        notes = []
        with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if line:
                    notes.append(json.loads(line))
        return notes

    def _save(self, notes):
        with open(self.path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for n in notes:
                f.write(json.dumps(n, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

    # ----- operations -----------------------------------------------------
    def add(self, title, body, tags=()):
        notes = self._load()
        nid = max((n["id"] for n in notes), default=0) + 1
        notes.append({
            "id": nid,
            "title": title,
            "body": body,
            "created_at": _now_iso(),
            "tags": list(tags),
            "archived": False,
        })
        self._save(notes)
        return nid

    def list_notes(self, tags=None, since=None, include_archived=False):
        notes = self._load()
        if not include_archived:
            notes = [n for n in notes if not _is_archived(n)]
        if tags:
            notes = [n for n in notes if _carries_all(n, tags)]
        if since is not None:
            try:
                since = date.fromisoformat(since).isoformat()
            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise ValueError(
                    "since must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD form, "
                    f"got {since!r}"
                ) from exc
            notes = [n for n in notes if _created_on_or_after(n, since)]
        return notes

    def find(self, text, include_archived=False):
        return [
            n for n in self._load()
            if (include_archived or not _is_archived(n))
            and (text in n["title"] or text in n["body"])
        ]

    def search(self, text, include_archived=False):
        """Case-insensitive text-and-tag search, in file order.

        A note is a hit when ``text``, ignoring case, appears as a substring
        of its title or body, or when it matches one of the note's tags.
        Tag comparison is forgiving -- the one place tags are not matched
        exactly: both the query and each stored tag are passed through
        ``_normalize_tag`` (lowercased, stripped, internal whitespace runs
        collapsed to "-"), and the normalized query needs only to appear
        within the normalized tag name. So searching "errand" finds notes
        tagged "errand", searching "PYTHON  3" or "python 3" finds a note
        tagged "python-3", a fragment like "python" finds that note too, and
        messy tags stored by older records still match. Archived notes are
        only returned when ``include_archived`` is True (same rule as find).
        """
        lowered = text.lower()
        tag_query = _normalize_tag(text)
        hits = []
        for n in self._load():
            if not include_archived and _is_archived(n):
                continue
            if lowered in n["title"].lower() or lowered in n["body"].lower():
                hits.append(n)
                continue
            if tag_query and any(
                    tag_query in _normalize_tag(t)
                    for t in n.get("tags", [])):
                hits.append(n)
        return hits

    def _set_archived(self, nid, archived):
        """Set the archived flag on note ``nid`` and persist the change.

        Rewrites the whole file (the intended style for this store).
        Raises KeyError when no note carries that id.
        """
        notes = self._load()
        for n in notes:
            if n["id"] == nid:
                n["archived"] = bool(archived)
                self._save(notes)
                return nid
        raise KeyError(nid)

    def archive(self, nid):
        """Mark note ``nid`` as archived.

        Archived notes are hidden from plain list/find until unarchived or
        until a listing asks to include them. Idempotent: archiving an
        already-archived note keeps it archived. Returns ``nid``; raises
        KeyError when no note carries that id.
        """
        return self._set_archived(nid, True)

    def unarchive(self, nid):
        """Clear the archived flag on note ``nid``.

        The note becomes visible to plain list/find again. Idempotent:
        unarchiving a note that is not archived leaves it that way. Returns
        ``nid``; raises KeyError when no note carries that id.
        """
        return self._set_archived(nid, False)

    def rename_tag(self, old, new):
        """Replace tag ``old`` with ``new`` on every note that carries it.

        Walks every note in the file, archived ones included: wherever a
        stored tag equals ``old`` exactly as stored, it is replaced with
        ``new`` exactly as given -- no cleanup, no case folding, no
        deduplication, so a note that also already carried ``new`` simply
        ends up with both spellings replaced to ``new``. Records written
        before tags existed have no "tags" key, carry no tags, and are left
        untouched. The file is rewritten only when at least one note
        actually changed; returns the number of notes that were changed
        (renaming a tag to itself changes nothing).
        """
        notes = self._load()
        changed = 0
        for note in notes:
            tags = note.get("tags")
            if not tags:
                continue
            updated = [new if tag == old else tag for tag in tags]
            if updated == tags:
                continue
            note["tags"] = updated
            changed += 1
        if changed:
            self._save(notes)
        return changed

"""Command-line interface for the notes store.

Usage:
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] add [--tag TAG ...] TITLE BODY
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] list [--tag TAG ...] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--all]
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] find TEXT [--all]
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] search TEXT [--all]
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] rename-tag OLD NEW
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] archive ID
    python -m notes.cli [--file NOTES.jsonl] unarchive ID

Design notes:
  * ``--file`` (default: notes.jsonl in the current directory) is the
    supported way to point the CLI at a different notes file; keep it working.
  * ``add --tag`` is repeatable; each tag is stored on the note exactly as
    given — no normalization or cleanup.
  * ``list --tag TAG`` (repeatable) shows only notes carrying every given
    tag, compared exactly against the stored tag strings (nothing is
    normalized on either side), so ``'API Design'`` and ``'api-design'``
    select different notes. ``list`` with no --tag keeps showing all notes.
  * ``list --since YYYY-MM-DD`` shows only notes created on or after that
    date, compared against the date part of the note's ``created_at`` field;
    ``list`` with no --since keeps showing all notes.
  * ``search TEXT`` matches case-insensitively against title and body
    (substring) and also against tags: the text is compared to the note's
    tags with the forgiving matching search has always used — the text and
    each stored tag are normalized for the comparison and the normalized
    text need only appear within the normalized tag (a tag's name, a messy
    spelling, or a fragment of either all match). This forgiving rule is
    search-only and unchanged; add/list match tags exactly.
    Archived notes are left out unless ``--all`` is passed. ``find`` keeps
    its original exact-case title/body behavior.
  * ``rename-tag OLD NEW`` renames a tag on every note in the file,
    archived ones included: wherever a stored tag equals OLD exactly as
    stored, it is replaced with NEW exactly as typed (no cleanup, no case
    folding), and the command prints how many notes were changed. Records
    without a ``tags`` key carry no tags and are untouched. The comparison
    is exact like add/list; search's forgiving tag matching is unaffected.
  * ``archive ID`` / ``unarchive ID`` flip the note's ``archived`` flag.
    ``list`` and ``find`` hide archived notes by default; ``--all`` on
    either command includes them again. archive/unarchive act by id and work
    whether or not the note is currently archived; a missing id is an error.
  * Notes print one line per note as "[<id>] <title> :: <body>"; keep the
    one-line-per-note shape so output stays grep-able.
"""
import argparse

from .store import NoteStore


def print_notes(notes):
    for n in notes:
        print(f"[{n['id']}] {n['title']} :: {n['body']}")


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="notes")
    parser.add_argument("--file", default="notes.jsonl")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_add = sub.add_parser("add", help="add a note")
    p_add.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[],
                       metavar="TAG", help="tag the note (repeatable)")
    p_add.add_argument("title")
    p_add.add_argument("body")

    p_list = sub.add_parser("list", help="list notes")
    p_list.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=None,
                        metavar="TAG",
                        help="only show notes carrying this tag (repeatable)")
    p_list.add_argument("--since", metavar="YYYY-MM-DD", default=None,
                        help="only show notes created on or after this date")
    p_list.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                        help="include archived notes")

    p_find = sub.add_parser("find", help="find notes by substring")
    p_find.add_argument("text")
    p_find.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                        help="include archived notes")

    p_search = sub.add_parser(
        "search", help="search notes (case-insensitive; matches tags too)")
    p_search.add_argument("text")
    p_search.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                          help="include archived notes")

    p_rename_tag = sub.add_parser(
        "rename-tag", help="rename a tag on every note (archived too)")
    p_rename_tag.add_argument("old", metavar="OLD",
                              help="tag to rename (exact stored form)")
    p_rename_tag.add_argument("new", metavar="NEW",
                              help="replacement tag (stored exactly as typed)")

    p_archive = sub.add_parser("archive", help="archive a note by id")
    p_archive.add_argument("id", type=int, metavar="ID",
                           help="id of the note to archive")

    p_unarchive = sub.add_parser("unarchive", help="unarchive a note by id")
    p_unarchive.add_argument("id", type=int, metavar="ID",
                             help="id of the note to unarchive")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    store = NoteStore(args.file)

    if args.cmd == "add":
        nid = store.add(args.title, args.body, tags=args.tag)
        print(f"added {nid}")
    elif args.cmd == "list":
        try:
            print_notes(store.list_notes(tags=args.tag, since=args.since,
                                         include_archived=args.all))
        except ValueError as exc:
            parser.error(str(exc))
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        print_notes(store.find(args.text, include_archived=args.all))
    elif args.cmd == "search":
        print_notes(store.search(args.text, include_archived=args.all))
    elif args.cmd == "rename-tag":
        changed = store.rename_tag(args.old, args.new)
        print(f"renamed {changed} notes")
    elif args.cmd == "archive":
        try:
            store.archive(args.id)
        except KeyError:
            parser.error(f"no note with id {args.id}")
        print(f"archived {args.id}")
    elif args.cmd == "unarchive":
        try:
            store.unarchive(args.id)
        except KeyError:
            parser.error(f"no note with id {args.id}")
        print(f"unarchived {args.id}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# notes

A tiny JSONL-backed note-taking CLI, used as a teaching toy.

Current capabilities:

    python -m notes.cli add [--tag TAG ...] "title" "body"               # append a note
    python -m notes.cli list [--tag TAG ...] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--all] # show notes
    python -m notes.cli find TEXT [--all]                                # substring match in title/body
    python -m notes.cli search TEXT [--all]                              # case-insensitive text & tag search
    python -m notes.cli rename-tag OLD NEW                               # rename a tag across every note
    python -m notes.cli archive ID                                       # hide a note
    python -m notes.cli unarchive ID                                     # show a note again

Notes carry tags: `add --tag TAG` is repeatable and stores each tag in the
note's `tags` list exactly as given (an empty list when no `--tag` is
given). `list --tag TAG` is also repeatable and shows only notes carrying
every given tag, compared exactly against the stored strings — so
`'API Design'` and `'api-design'` are different tags. Plain `list` still
shows all notes.

Nothing rewrites a note's tags on its own: a note tagged while the old
normalization was active keeps its cleaned spelling (e.g. `api-design`) on
disk, and `list --tag api-design` finds it by that exact stored form. The
only way stored tags change is the explicit rename below.

`rename-tag OLD NEW` renames a tag across every note in the file, archived
ones included, and prints how many notes were changed. The match is exact —
wherever a stored tag equals `OLD` exactly as stored, it is replaced with
`NEW` exactly as typed: no cleanup, no case folding, so `'API Design'` and
`'api-design'` stay distinct unless you rename one spelling into the other.
Records written before `tags` existed carry no tags and are left alone.
Afterwards the renamed tag behaves like any other: `list --tag NEW` finds
the notes (with `--all` when they are archived), and `search` still
surfaces them via its forgiving tag matching.

Every note also records when it was created in a `created_at` field: an
ISO-8601 timestamp (local time with its UTC offset) stamped at add time.
`list --since YYYY-MM-DD` shows only notes created on or after that date,
compared against the date part of `created_at` (the date itself is
included). Records written before `created_at` existed have no timestamp and
never match a `--since` filter; plain `list` still shows all notes.

`search TEXT` finds notes whose title or body contains the text (substring
match, ignoring case) and also finds notes by tag: a note surfaces when the
search text matches one of its tags, with the same forgiving tag matching
search has always used — the text and each stored tag are normalized for
the comparison (lowercased, whitespace runs collapsed to `-`) and the
normalized text need only appear within the normalized tag name. So
`search 'PYTHON  3'` or `search 'python 3'` still finds a note tagged
`python-3`, a fragment such as `search 'python'` finds it too, and messy
spellings — from older records or from verbatim tags like `'API Design'` —
still match (e.g. `search 'api design'` finds a note tagged `'API Design'`).
This forgiving rule applies only inside search; `add` and `list --tag`
store and match tags exactly, as described above. Archived notes are left
out of search results unless `--all` is passed. The original `find TEXT`
keeps its exact, case-sensitive title/body behavior.

Every note has an `archived` flag (new notes start unarchived). `archive ID`
hides a note without deleting it; `unarchive ID` brings it back. Archived
notes are left out of plain `list` and `find`; pass `--all` to either
command to include them again. Records written before `archived` existed
have no flag and count as not archived. The flag composes with the other
filters, so e.g. `list --tag errand` also skips archived notes while
`list --all --tag errand` includes them.

Notes are stored one-JSON-object-per-line in `notes.jsonl` (override with
`--file`). See `notes/store.py` for the design notes. New features should add
fields to the note record rather than changing the storage format.
